verifier: Fact Integrity Auditor (PowerUP and product-doc pass)

claims.text: LLMs are stateless systems and do not retain prior prompts or responses by themselves.
claims.evidence: PowerUP foundations section describes LLMs as inherently stateless.

claims.text: An agent harness is the surrounding software infrastructure that manages context, tools, memory, state, execution environments, and feedback loops around an LLM.
Agent memory learns about a user from prior conversations and activity across connected enterprise systems.
claims.evidence: PowerUP definition of agent memory and current Memory documentation.

claims.text: The PowerUP distinguishes short-term memory from long-term procedural, semantic, and episodic memory.
Procedural memory is knowing how a user gets work done, semantic memory is knowing durable facts, and episodic memory is remembering when.
Short-term memory includes session-based working context; long-term memory carries useful context across sessions and time.
claims.evidence: PowerUP short-term/long-term taxonomy and Memory documentation.

claims.text: Glean’s session log writer reads assistant traces including conversation history, tool calls, outputs, decisions, failures, and user corrections.
Glean’s activity snapshot agent extracts agent-relevant memories from enterprise activity independently of assistant usage.
A consolidation agent reads session and activity outputs and pushes them into long-term memory; the PowerUP says new context is consolidated daily.
claims.evidence: PowerUP Engram write and limitations slides.

claims.text: At run time, a small high-signal memory summary can be placed in the system prompt.
claims.evidence: PowerUP Engram read slide and Memory documentation.

claims.text: At run time, Glean selectively retrieves relevant sections of memory files, daily logs, and snapshots using progressive disclosure.
claims.evidence: PowerUP Engram read slide and current agent-building guidance.

claims.text: The PowerUP presents personal memory management as user-controlled: users can view, edit, and delete memory details.
The PowerUP positions Glean as a centrally governed memory layer across Glean Assistant, connected apps, and third-party AI tools through Gateway or MCP patterns.

The PowerUP states that current support for agent Memory is for Glean hosted and Glean Key customers, that new context may take about a day to appear, and that this differs from the per-step Memory field in Workflow Agent builder.
Current product documentation should be checked before making a customer commitment about Memory behavior or availability.
claims.evidence: Studio sourcing rule: current product documentation is primary authority for product behavior.
